title: SBProxy Security
description: Security metrics including WAF blocks, rate limiting, authentication failures, IP filtering, bot detection, CORS refusals, RFC 9421 legacy signature derivation, and certificate-store degradation.

panels.title: WAF Blocks/sec
panels.description: Measures WAF Blocks/sec. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#security-controls. When red, inspect the matching component, confirm healthy range, and follow the rollback guidance if the spike follows a config change.

panels.title: Rate Limit Hits
panels.description: Measures Rate Limit Hits. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#security-controls. When red, inspect the matching component, confirm healthy range, and follow the rollback guidance if the spike follows a config change.

panels.title: Auth Failures by Type
panels.description: Auth refusals per second, split by the provider that decided. `sbproxy_auth_results_total` labels its result `allow` or `deny`; this panel read `failure`, a value nothing has ever written, and drew an empty graph over every refusal the gateway made (corrected in WOR-2667).

panels.title: IP Filter Blocks
panels.description: Measures IP Filter Blocks. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#security-controls. When red, inspect the matching component, confirm healthy range, and follow the rollback guidance if the spike follows a config change.

panels.title: Bot Detections
panels.description: Measures Bot Detections. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#security-controls. When red, inspect the matching component, confirm healthy range, and follow the rollback guidance if the spike follows a config change.

panels.title: Key Operations
panels.description: Admin key-lifecycle operations (mint, update, delete, revoke, block, unblock, rotate) by real handler outcome. `refused` is a 4xx the operator can act on; `error` is the store or governance backend failing and belongs with the key-store outage panels. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#security-controls.

panels.title: Credential Resolution Latency
panels.description: Bound-credential resolution p95 plus the two series that should read zero: stale grace serves (a backend failure wearing a grace period) and outright resolution errors. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#security-controls.

panels.title: Key Lookup Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description: Two distinct caches, deliberately on one panel so they cannot be conflated: the keystore TTL cache in front of the store (key + credential record lookups) and the per-generation resolved-secret cache in front of the vault round-trip. A falling TTL-cache ratio hammers the store; a falling resolved-secret ratio hammers the secret backend. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#security-controls.

panels.title: Audit Write Failures
panels.description: Audit emissions that did not reach a sink they were promised, by channel: audit.key_path is the key and credential mutation trail, audit.admin_path is the admin-console action trail. Reads exactly zero in a healthy system; any nonzero value means the tamper-evident trail has a hole that cannot be backfilled, and SBPROXY-AUDIT-WRITE-FAILURE pages on the same condition across all audit channels. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#rb-audit-write.

panels.title: Certificate Store Degraded

matcher.options: no certificate store opened in this scrape

targets.legendFormat: no certificate store opened in this scrape

panels.description: 1 when this process could not open the certificate-store backend named by acme.storage_backend and is running on an in-memory store, 0 when the configured backend opened. Only the pod-local backends (redb, sqlite, memory) can reach 1: a shared backend (file, redis, s3, gcs, azure) that will not open refuses to start instead, so a fleet cannot silently lose the ACME issuance lock. At 1, certificates do not survive a restart, so every restart opens a fresh ACME order and a restart loop burns the CA's duplicate-certificate limit for the hostname set. Fix acme.storage_path or the backend and restart the pod. The gauge is written once at startup, so it moves only across a restart. The second series reads 1 when nothing in the scrape has opened a certificate store at all, which is expected with no ACME configured and is not the same as a healthy 0. SBPROXY-CERT-STORE-DEGRADED alerts on the same condition. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#rb-cert-store-degraded.

panels.title: CORS Refusals by Reason
panels.description: Responses the CORS middleware refused to add headers to, by reason. The only reason today is wildcard_with_credentials: a live config still pairs allowed_origins: ["*"] with allow_credentials: true, which browsers reject, so those calls are failing in the browser rather than at the proxy. Name the origins explicitly, or drop allow_credentials, and reload. A new config fails to compile on this pairing, so a line here is a config applied before that check existed and still running. No data is the healthy state: the series only appears once a refusal has happened. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#security-controls.

panels.title: RFC 9421 Legacy Signature Derivation
panels.description: RFC 9421 signatures that verified only against the pre-conformance derivation of @target-uri or @request-target, by component. Accepting the old derivation is a deprecation window and will be removed, so every request on this line is a peer that breaks when it closes. Find the signer from the once-per-process warn line, which carries the verifier's own key id, and move it to a conformant RFC 9421 library. No data means no peer is still on the old derivation. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#security-controls.

panels.title: Legacy Signature Derivations (24h)
panels.description: Legacy-derivation acceptances over the last 24 hours, per component. This is the number that decides whether the compatibility fallback can be removed: close the window once both components hold at zero across a full traffic cycle, weekly and monthly batch callers included, not just across one quiet afternoon. Anything above zero means at least one signer has not moved yet. No alert fires on this: a deprecation counter is a planning input, not a page. Runbook: docs/operator-runbook.md#security-controls.

panels.title: External Authorization Outcomes
panels.description: Every `ext_authz` callout, by what came back. `fail_open` is the one to alert on: those requests were admitted without the authorization service deciding anything, because the callout failed and the origin is configured with `failure_mode_allow: true`. `unavailable` is the same failure refusing instead of admitting. Absent until an origin configures an `ext_authz` provider.

panels.title: Token Introspection Results
panels.description: RFC 7662 introspection results per second. `cached` is a verdict the local cache answered without reaching the authorization server, so the ratio of `cached` to everything else is what `cache_ttl` is buying. `unavailable` means the server could not be reached and the request was refused with a 503. Absent until an origin configures an `oauth_introspection` provider.

panels.title: Agent Identity Verdicts (KYA)
panels.description: Know Your Agent token verification, by verdict. `revoked` and `expired` are agents presenting credentials their issuer has withdrawn; `insufficient_balance` is a verified agent refused because its spend balance is below the origin's floor; `directory_unavailable` means the issuer's JWKS or denylist could not be fetched and no cached copy was still inside its stale-grace window. Absent until an origin configures a `kya` provider.

panels.title: Behavioral Anomalies
panels.description: Observations the anomaly detector put in the long tail for their agent class, by kind and severity. `ja4_outlier` is a TLS fingerprint the class has essentially never presented; `headless_library` is a headless browser showing up where one does not belong, and never reports below `warn`; `request_rate_spike` is one address far past its class's per-address mean. Absent until `proxy.anomaly.enabled` is true, and quiet for a while after every restart: the window is in memory, so a deploy costs the detector its baseline and it says nothing until it has re-learned one.

panels.title: Agent Reputation
panels.description: Reputation per tenant and agent class, 1.0 down to 0.0, over the detector's rolling 28-day window. A critical verdict costs five times a warning, and weight decays by rolling out of the window rather than on a timer, so a class that stops misbehaving recovers on its own; the gauge is republished on every analysis, not only when a verdict fires, so the number moves while the class recovers. A class that goes entirely silent keeps its last score until it sends again. Advisory unless an operator sets proxy.anomaly.reputation.deny_below or challenge_below, which turn it into an admission decision.

panels.title: Anomaly Detector Capacity
panels.description: How many (tenant, agent class) windows the detector holds, against its cap of 512, and how often a request arrived for a class it had no slot for. The resident set is the key count times the per-key window, so this is the line to size the process against. A non-zero budget rate means windows are being displaced, which churns the baseline a reputation.deny_below floor reads: a class with no window has no score, and no score is admitted.

panels.title: MCP grant expiry
panels.description: Time-boxed MCP RBAC grants that elapsed, by tenant and policy. A rise means reviewed access is still being used after its window closed, and the matching tools/call is being refused until an operator renews it.

panels.title: MCP approval holds
panels.description: High-risk MCP tool calls parked for an operator, by tenant. The caller's connection is not held open; a retry after approve consumes the snapshot once.

panels.title: Credential Read Audit (WOR-2570)
panels.description: Volume against detail. `sbproxy_credential_read_total` moves on every credential resolution including cached ones; the chained detail record fires at most once per credential per `key_management.read_audit.detail_window_secs`, and the reads that did not get one are counted `suppressed`. The two series diverging is the design, not a fault: cost scales with credential count, not request rate. A detail rate of zero while reads climb means `read_audit.enabled` is off, or (if it is on) the fingerprint key is missing and records are being refused rather than emitted in the clear, which shows as `failed`. Runbook: docs/key-management.md#read-and-access-audit.

panels.title: Root of Trust Liveness (WOR-2568)
panels.description: Whether the customer's key service still answers and still authorizes this proxy. A zero on `sbproxy_root_of_trust_liveness` stops credential decryption immediately: the failed probe drops the cached data keys and every credential this root had opened, so the wait is the probe interval rather than `key_management.crypto.root_of_trust.unwrap_cache_ttl_secs`, which is the worst case with no probe running. Note that the series is only written by the probe itself, so `liveness_interval_secs: 0` leaves it absent and this panel cannot alert. That is the intended outcome after a customer revokes their grant, and an incident otherwise; check `GET /admin/crypto/root-of-trust` to tell them apart. The `unwrap` to `unwrap_cached` ratio is what the cache is actually buying, and the absolute `unwrap` rate is what the key service's own rate limit is sized against. Runbook: docs/key-management.md#customer-managed-root-of-trust.

panels.title: Break-Glass Grants (WOR-2573)
panels.description: The emergency path, and whether anyone is reviewing it. `awaiting_review` is the number a security reviewer opens this dashboard for: a grant that expired with nobody signing off on what was done under it. Alert when `sbproxy_break_glass_open{state="awaiting_review"}` stays above zero for longer than `key_management.break_glass.review_window_secs`. A `used` rate that outruns `reviewed` over any window is the same finding stated as a rate. Runbook: docs/key-management.md#break-glass-emergency-access.

panels.title: Rotation Age (WOR-2567)
panels.description: Days since the oldest record of each kind was minted or rotated, published when `GET /admin/credentials` is listed. Compare against the crypto period named in `key_management.crypto.rotation`: 90 days for credentials and inbound keys by default, following NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev 5. This is what turns "rotate periodically" into a page. A flat line means nothing is listing the admin API, not that nothing is ageing. Runbook: docs/key-management.md#rotation-cadence.

panels.title: GeoIP Lookups
panels.description: Measures geoip policy lookups by outcome (hit, miss, no_database, no_client_ip). Runbook: docs/request-enrichment.md. A rising no_database share means the origin has geoip configured with no reachable MMDB.

panels.title: User-Agent Headless Detections
panels.description: Measures user_agent_parser headless-automation-library detections and overall device_type mix. Runbook: docs/request-enrichment.md. A sudden headless_chrome/puppeteer/selenium spike against a flat device_type total is worth correlating with the JA4 headless_signal in sbproxy-security.json's Bot Detections panel.
